description: Imports Notion workspace users, databases, pages, page blocks, and comments via the Notion REST API.

authTierRationale: The 'token' credential branch needs only a single self-serve access token from an internal Notion integration, sent as a bearer header — T1_SIMPLE. The alternative OAuth2.0 branch is T2_BYO_APP: its spec marks client_id, client_secret and access_token all as required, so a standalone user must register their own public Notion integration; no refresh token is requested or stored (Notion access tokens do not expire), so it never reaches T3. Estuary's hosted control plane can supply the OAuth app itself — the connector ships a flow.OAuth2Spec with provider 'notion' and templated authorize/token URLs and a Basic client_id:client_secret token-exchange header — but the standalone tier is what is scored here. authTierOverall is the easiest mode: T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: For every incremental Notion stream the backfill and incremental legs issue byte-identical HTTP requests. There is no server-side time filter at all: /search is only sorted ascending by last_edited_time, and record dropping against state and start_date happens client-side in parse_response. The schema's backfill/incremental split therefore duplicates one pull shape and cannot express 'the filter is applied after the response'.

page_size is not a constant. It starts at 100, is halved (floor 10) on every HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout, and is restored to 100 on the next 200. A static pageSize int cannot express an adaptive page size.

blocks is not a one-level parent/child substream: it recurses depth-first into itself, re-requesting blocks/{id}/children for any record with has_children, up to depth 30. pathPlaceholders describes a flat parent scope and cannot express self-recursion or its depth cap.

page_last_edited_time is not a field the API returns; the connector injects the parent page's last_edited_time onto each comment record because comment ordering across pages is not guaranteed. The schema has no way to mark a cursor field as connector-synthesized.

The connector's runtime auth for the OAuth branch is still a plain bearer header on credentials.access_token; the oauth2 scheme member describes only how that token is obtained (by the control plane or the user), not how it is sent. Both facts matter and only one fits.

This is an Airbyte-shimmed connector: neither the connector nor estuary_cdk/shim_airbyte_cdk.py encodes any interval or cron. Cadence is decided entirely by the Flow runtime outside the connector, so every schedule field is empty rather than merely unknown.

defaultSchedule.description: cadence owned by the runtime, not the connector

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Neither source-notion nor estuary_cdk/shim_airbyte_cdk.py contains any interval, cron, or duration literal; the shim's ResourceConfig exposes only stream/syncMode/namespace/cursorField. Cadence is set by the Flow runtime outside the connector, so no connector-level default exists to record.
abstained.streams[].schedules: Same reason: no per-binding schedule is expressible in the shim ResourceConfig, so the list is empty rather than guessed.
abstained.credentialModes[1].scheme.scopes: The Notion authorize URL template built in __main__.py passes only client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, owner=user and state. No `scope` parameter is sent and the spec declares none, so the scope list is left empty rather than invented.
abstained.streams[0].cursorField: Users derives from NotionStream, not IncrementalNotionStream, and declares no cursor_field; the discover snapshot and test.flow.yaml both give it syncMode full_refresh with no cursorField.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.incrementalParam: Null for every stream by evidence, not by uncertainty: no request parameter or body field carries the cursor. /search is only sorted ascending on last_edited_time, and records below state/start_date are dropped in parse_response after the response arrives.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Recorded as `merge` because the shim always emits op="u" documents against keyed collections (destination_sync_mode="append", Flow reduces by key), including for the full_refresh `users` binding. No tombstone or delete document is ever produced by this connector, so deleted Notion objects are never removed downstream. Marked medium confidence because the disposition is a property of the shim/Flow runtime rather than anything source-notion states.
abstained.streams[1].pull.backfill / streams[2..4]: Populated with the same PullSpec as the incremental leg because the connector issues an identical request in both cases (full_refresh merely sets stream_state to None). Recorded at medium confidence: the two legs are not distinguishable in the source.
abstained.execution.continuity: Null and deliberately so: this is a pure poll-mode HTTP connector. It creates no server-side artifact in the customer's Notion workspace (no webhook registration, subscription, or scratch object), nothing accrues on Notion's side if we stop between ticks, and nothing is lost on ours — resumption re-runs /search and /users from scratch and only the client-side last_edited_time watermark advances. The only pause-sensitive value is the per-page `start_cursor`, which is held in memory for the duration of one sweep and never checkpointed across runs.
